meta.parties: Sheriff v. Pitche Umma Et Al

rules.statement: For a conviction of criminal trespass to be valid, the re-entry must not only have been made in assertion of a right known to the law but also with intent to annoy the complainant. If these conditions are not met, the charge fails.
rules.supporting_quote: "As Straight J. said in In re Govind Prassad [ 2 (1879) 2 All. 465.]: ' Re-entry into or remaining upon land from which a person has been ejected by civil process or of which possession has been given to another, for the purpose of asserting rights he may have solely or jointly with others, is not criminal trespass, unless the intent to commit an offence or to intimidate insult, or annoy is conclusively proved.'"
